title.en: Japan protests against Putin visit to disputed islands
title.zh: 日本抗议普京访问争议岛屿

summary.en: Japan has formally protested Russia's President Vladimir Putin's visit to the Kuril Islands, a territory disputed by both nations, marking his first visit there according to Russian state media.
summary.zh: 据俄罗斯官方媒体报道，日本已就俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京首次访问两国存在争议的千岛群岛（日本称北方四岛）一事提出抗议。

body.en:
Japan said it "strongly protests" Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to a disputed island chain.

Russian state media reported on Thursday that Putin visited Iturup - known in Japan as Etorofu - one of four islands in the Kuril chain that are claimed by both Russia and Japan.

Japan's foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi said the islands are "inherently Japanese territory both historically and under international law, and the Government of Japan strongly protests this visit".

The two countries have been locked in a dispute over the Kuril islands for decades.

This dispute was the main reason Moscow and Tokyo did not sign a peace treaty after World War Two.

The Kuril islands sit between Hokkaido in northern Japan and Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. Four of the southernmost islands are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.

They are administered by Russia. At the end of World War Two, the Soviet Union annexed the island chain and deported around 17,000 Japanese residents.

During his visit on Thursday, Putin sampled fish roe and spoke to island locals, Russian state media reported.

The islands are strategic spots for Russia's military operations, with Iturup being used as its primary military air base in the region.

Last month, Chinese and Russian naval warships sailed through a strait in the Kuril islands during a joint patrol.

Russia also held military drills near the islands last year, drawing condemnation from Japan.
body.zh: 日本表示“强烈抗议”俄罗斯总统普京访问有争议的岛链。 俄罗斯官方媒体周四报道称，普京访问了伊图鲁普岛——在日本被称为择捉岛——俄罗斯和日本均声称拥有主权的千岛链上的四个岛屿之一。 日本外务大臣茂木敏充表示，这些岛屿“无论在历史上还是在国际法上都是日本固有领土，日本政府强烈抗议这次访问”。 几十年来，两国围绕千岛群岛一直存在争议。 这一争端是莫斯科和东京在第二次世界大战后未能签署和平条约的主要原因。 千岛群岛位于日本北部的北海道和俄罗斯堪察加半岛之间。日本声称对最南端的四个岛屿拥有主权，称其为北方四岛。 它们由俄罗斯管理。第二次世界大战结束时，苏联吞并了该岛链并驱逐了约 17,000 名日本居民。 据俄罗斯官方媒体报道，普京在周四访问期间品尝了鱼子，并与岛上当地人进行了交谈。 这些岛屿是俄罗斯军事行动的战略要地，伊图鲁普被用作俄罗斯在该地区的主要军事空军基地。 上个月，中国和俄罗斯海军军舰在联合巡逻中穿过千岛群岛的一个海峡。 俄罗斯去年也在这些岛屿附近举行了军事演习，引起了日本的谴责。

title.en: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
title.zh: 诺贝尔和平奖获得者告诉BBC，普京不能再宣称在乌克兰获胜

summary.en: In an exclusive interview with the BBC’s Steve Rosenberg, Dmitry Muratov says the Kremlin leader can only "destroy Ukraine, not conquer it", with the war now in its fifth year.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Mr Muratov co-founded Novaya Gazeta more than thirty years ago. It became the flagship for hard-hitting independent journalism in Russia, shining a light on human rights abuses and high-level corruption.

In 2021 Mr Muratov was joint winner of the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts "to safeguard freedom of expression." The Nobel Committee noted that "six of [Novaya Gazeta's] journalists have been killed, including Anna Politkovskaya who wrote revealing articles on the war in Chechnya."

"Putin issued a decree and the newspaper's printing presses were nationalised," Mr Muratov explains. "Its registration was revoked."

Novaya Gazeta does retain a presence online. But only just: the authorities have blocked access to its website. It can only be accessed from abroad, or with the help of VPNs – virtual private networks used to circumvent restrictions.

The newspaper's difficulties reflect the broader crackdown on free speech in Russia which has accelerated since the Kremlin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

"Most opinion leaders have been declared 'foreign agents', 'extremists' or 'terrorists'. Several hundred," says Dmitry Muratov.

"Figures vary, but at a conservative estimate, since the start of Russia's 'special military operation' [in Ukraine] at least 1,500 people are now in prison having spoken out against current state policy. That's three times more than during the savage days of the KGB in the USSR."

In his 1975 Nobel Peace Prize lecture dissident Andrei Sakharov listed the names of more than 120 political prisoners he was aware of in the Soviet Union. A decade later Amnesty International estimated more than 600 prisoners of conscience in the USSR.

What the Kremlin had assumed in 2022 would be a short, successful "military operation" has become the bloodiest conflict in Europe since the Second World War.

"There will never be 'victory'," counters Dmitry Muratov. "Because what has been going on for nearly five years – no matter how it ends – can no longer be considered a victory.

"It cannot be a victory when two Slavic nations have ripped a million people to shreds. Or more than a million."

"It seems to me that the situation with Ukraine now is this: you can destroy it, but you cannot conquer it. What do I mean by destroy? Continued escalation all the way to the use of a nuclear weapon."

Does he really believe the Kremlin leader would use nuclear weapons in this war?

"All those political experts who say 'Putin thinks this' or 'Putin is scared of that'…they're all charlatans," claims Dmitry Muratov. "It's in the same league as astrology. Nobody knows what's going on in Vladimir Putin's head. And I don't know.

"I see things only as a journalist. I study big data. And since the beginning of the year the need to use nuclear weapons...

title.en: BTS star V reveals hearing loss battle during livestream
title.zh: BTS 明星 V 在直播中透露听力损失之战

summary.en: The K-pop star says he has suffered hearing issues for over two years before revealing it publicly this week.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
V, a member of pop sensation BTS, says he has been receiving treatment for hearing loss in one ear, an announcement that comes midway through the band's highly-anticipated world tour.

In a livestream on Wednesday, the 30-year-old said that he has dealt with the problem for about two and a half years. This was the first time he was revealing it to the band's fans, he said.

"If the hearing in my left ear is at 100, it's only about 30 in my right," said V, whose real name is Kim Tae-hyung.

The band is currently on its first world tour in years, marking the reunion of all seven members since they went on a hiatus for mandatory military service.

During the livestream, V said his hearing became worse when he was serving in the military.

But he said he did not take it seriously at first, believing it to be "a matter of mental strength".

With rare exceptions, all able-bodied men are required to serve 18 months of military service in South Korea.

This included BTS members, who were at the height of their fame in 2022 when they started taking career breaks to enlist in the military.

The Arirang World Tour, which kicked off in April in South Korea, marked the highly-anticipated reunion of the band's seven members.

The livestream on Wednesday came after the band wrapped its concerts in Baltimore, Maryland.

V was joined by his bandmate Jungkook, who talked about a shin injury he has been dealing with during the tour, saying he was "on the verge of developing a stress fracture".

Jungkook added that he would have to manage his injury well in order to keep performing.

In the coming months, the concert tour will take BTS to cities around the world, including Los Angeles, Buenos Aires, Bangkok, Sydney and Hong Kong.

title.en: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
title.zh: 乌克兰袭击黑海港口，俄罗斯主要粮食出口码头受损

summary.en: Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are falling as both countries attack each other's shipping facilities and ports.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯和乌克兰相互袭击对方的航运设施和港口，导致两国粮食出口均出现下降。

body.en:
A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port of Novorossiysk has damaged two major grain export terminals and hit the last big Russian naval base on the Black Sea, reports say.

Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and another 24 injured in the overnight attack, local officials said.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv had launched rockets, jet and naval drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian base, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit.

Ukraine's military later said four Russian warships, including two frigates, were hit. Russia has not commented on the issue.

"The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelensky said in a post on social media.

Most of Russia's Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk - one of the largest ports in Russia - after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks.

The attack follows an uptick in the exchange of strikes in the Black Sea this summer, after a period of relative calm.

In an interview with CNN, Zelensky said that Ukraine needs a tenth of the current US stockpile of interceptor missiles to stop all Russian ballistic missile attacks.

"This year we have two and a half times less interceptors than we had in 2025," the Ukrainian president said.

A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia's TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit in the attack on Wednesday, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same.

The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes. It did not make any reference to Ukraine's attacks but said it was "taking into account current logistical constraints".

Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects.

An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city.

Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by "several hundred drones" overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes.

For its part, Moscow launched aerial overnight strikes which killed at least 11 civilians in Ukraine between Tuesday and Wednesday.

The majority were killed when Russia hit the southern city of Zaporizhzhia with ballistic missiles and glide bombs.

title.en: Twitch users can now block Amazon from using their content to train AI
title.zh: Twitch用户现在可以阻止亚马逊使用其内容训练人工智能

summary.en: Streaming platform Twitch has introduced a new feature allowing its users to opt out of having their channel content used by Amazon for training artificial intelligence. This change comes after users expressed criticism regarding the company's initial policy on AI training data.
summary.zh: 直播平台Twitch推出了一项新功能，允许用户选择不让亚马逊将其频道内容用于训练人工智能。此举是在用户对该公司最初的人工智能训练数据政策提出批评后推出的。

body.en:
Twitch is now allowing users to stop Amazon from training their generative artificial intelligence (AI) models using users' content, the popular streaming platform said.

The US company said users can opt out of a default setting that allows Amazon to use streams, clips, images, chats and other channel content.

The announcement on Wednesday confirmed that the technology giant, which took over Twitch in 2014, was using the platform's content for AI training, prompting widespread backlash from users.

Amazon runs a host of AI services and has heavily invested in the its development as it seeks to compete with Google, Meta and other technology giants.

Twitch is a major livestreaming platform that is especially popular among gamers and youths. The platform's top content creators have tens of millions of followers.

AI training collection has been turned on by default just as it is on most content services, but Twitch is "respecting" users' wishes to opt out if they prefer, Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton said during a stream on the platform , external .

Asked why data is being collected by default, he said: "If it's opt-in, nobody would opt-in. That's the honest answer."

Users who remain opted in could have any of their channel content used for training, Minton said, adding that the data collected will not be re-sold to other companies.

During the same session, Mary Kish, head of community at Twitch, took viewers through a tutorial on how to disable generative AI training through a user's channel settings.

"We don't expect you to be happy or excited about this. I don't expect anyone to react to this favourably," she added.

The stream's chat column was flooded with hundreds of comments from users criticising the move.

One viewer wrote: "Nobody would opt in because nobody wants to feed AI with our creativity and content."

Another said Twitch had an "opportunity to set an industry standard" to push back against data collection for AI.

It is not clear when Amazon began collecting Twitch users' data to train its AI models.

Minton said during the stream that he did not know if users' data had already been scraped for training, adding that he was unsure what Amazon "has done in terms of model training and what they've used and not used."

title.en: Trump's fiercest defender? Five moments defining Karoline Leavitt's time as press secretary
title.zh: 特朗普最激烈的捍卫者？卡罗琳·莱维特担任新闻秘书期间的五个时刻

summary.en: Few figures in the Trump administration have been as visible — or loyal — as Karoline Leavitt.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Karoline Leavitt is leaving her post as White House press secretary after 20 months marked by fierce loyalty to United States President Donald Trump and fiery clashes with the media.

As Trump's highest-ranking spokesperson, the 28-year-old became known for her unwavering defences of the president, her embrace of MAGA and "new media" voices including podcasters and influencers, and her amplification of false, misleading and highly contentious claims from the podium.

Trump announced she was leaving her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family, and would continue to serve as one of his "top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party". Leavitt has two young children, the first born during Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and the second in May this year.

She was the first White House press secretary history to give birth while serving in the role, and the youngest person ever to hold the position.

Leavitt has been press secretary since Trump returned to office in January last year, making her the president's second-longest-serving press secretary after Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who served from 2017 to 2019.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Trump's next press secretary will be his sixth across two terms. He is yet to indicate who may replace Leavitt.

Leavitt and White House communications director Steven Cheung revamped the Trump administration's already-confrontational posture toward the media.

The Trump administration began handpicking which journalists would receive access to the president, overhauling the long-running system established by the independent White House Correspondents Association.

The "press pool" was traditionally a rotation chosen by the industry group to ensure media outlets had uniform access to the president and could relay his activities to the public and to other journalists who could not attend smaller gatherings.

In one of Leavitt's first moves as press secretary last year, she introduced a "new media seat" in the White House briefing room. Continuing Trump's longstanding attacks on establishment journalists, she vowed to give new media voices a more prominent role in covering his presidency.

"We welcome independent journalists, podcasters, social media influencers and content creators to apply for credentials to cover this White House," she said in January 2025.

body.en:
Eurovision Song Contest organisers announced overnight they were excluding any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the competition and increased the minimum age of competitors.

While they did not mention any country by name, Israel, which has been at war in Gaza since 2023 , came close to winning the competition in both 2025 and 2026, ultimately finishing second on each occasion.

Under the old rules, the winning country normally hosts the following year's competition.

Under the new rules, "the winning broadcaster will automatically be ineligible to host the contest if an armed conflict, a sensitive geopolitical situation, or any other situation materially affects the security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region", the organisers said in a statement.

In a first, five countries — Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Iceland — boycotted the 2026 competition in Vienna over Israel's participation.

They said they could not take part alongside Israel because of its war in Gaza .

A United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the UN as a whole and has been criticised by Israel, concluded in September 2025 that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Israel is separately defending a genocide case at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), which has ordered Israel to implement provisional measures to ensure genocidal actions are not committed in Gaza, but has yet to issue a final ruling.

Martin Green, director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said in a statement that the changes had been guided by feedback from member countries.

He added: "These changes are about giving everyone involved greater clarity, protecting artists and ensuring the contest continues to provide a safe and welcoming environment, while preserving the spirit and integrity that make the Eurovision Song Contest so special."

The organisers also announced that competitors must be at least 18, up from 16, on the day of their first rehearsal.

"This change continues the work already undertaken by the contest to strengthen safeguarding and protect younger artists from the pressures associated with competing at the Eurovision Song Contest," they added in the statement.

The youngest person to win the contest was 13-year-old Sandra Kim from Belgium in 1986, according to Eurovision records.

Eurovision is a co-production of public broadcasters belonging to the European Broadcasting Union. Since the EBU includes members from outside Europe, the contest is not limited to European countries.

title.en: Israeli settlers keep up siege of Palestinian homes in West Bank after clashes with troops

body.en:
The Israeli military said overnight it would deploy additional troops to restore order after failing to end a blockade by Israeli settlers of Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank.

The siege began on Sunday, when settlers erected a makeshift tent near homes in the Palestinian village of Qusra, south of Nablus, preventing essential food and medical supplies from reaching residents.

Israeli troops clashed with the settlers while trying to disperse them from the outpost they set up directly in front of Palestinian homes, according to witnesses.

The incident marked a rare confrontation between settlers and the military and comes amid a sharp increase in settler land seizures and attacks on Palestinians.

All Israeli settlements and outposts in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law.

"We have received no food and no medicine," Qusai Abu Rida, a Palestinian trapped inside one of the houses, told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency by telephone, adding that he had only managed to secure electricity thanks to solar panels.

The Israeli military condemned the settlers' actions and declared the area a "closed military zone", removing their tent on Wednesday morning (local time).

By mid-afternoon, an AFP photographer at the scene said the military had left and the tent had been removed, but the settlers were still there.

"The army has withdrawn, and so far we are still besieged, with the settlers at our doorstep," he said.

Later on Wednesday, the military announced it would send an additional infantry battalion and that more soldiers would be on standby.

The chief of the general staff "directed that efforts to strengthen order and operational control in the area continue, as well as efforts to prevent further serious incidents", a military statement said.

A day earlier, the Israeli military said it had received reports of settlers entering and taking control of Palestinian homes and land in the area.

"This is illegal, reprehensible and unacceptable activity that harms the residents of the areas and disrupts their daily lives," it said.

It also said that disciplinary action would be taken against security personnel who had been filmed at the site days earlier.

Violence by Israeli settlers towards Palestinians in the West Bank has persisted for years , often with little or no legal consequence, but recent months have seen a surge in attacks .

Last Sunday, Israel's military closed the West Bank village of Taybeh to non-residents to prevent growing attacks on Palestinians by Israeli settlers. Taybeh is one of the only Christian villages remaining in the West Bank.

body.en:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who earned a reputation for acid putdowns of journalists, is to step down, United States President Donald Trump announced on Thursday AEST, adding she would remain a senior adviser.

Leavitt, 28, the youngest-ever US presidential spokesperson, has been a fiercely loyal Trump defender, delivering fluent and aggressive performances at often combative press briefings.

"Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides , Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family," Trump said on social media.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party."

In May, Leavitt announced the birth of her second child — a girl named Viviana — just days after delaying her maternity leave following an alleged assassination attempt on Trump when a gunman tried to storm the White House Correspondents' Dinner .

Her departure comes as Trump faces steadily sinking poll numbers and the Republican Party risks defeat in the November midterm congressional elections.

"I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium," Leavitt said on social media as her departure was announced.

"I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump’s successes."

Leavitt wrote that, after returning to the White House following the birth of her daughter, "I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve" while devoting the attention needed as press secretary.

Leavitt is a Trump veteran who served in his press office during his first term that ended in 2021 and then as his spokesperson during his 2024 election campaign.

Leavitt's tenure as press secretary saw a revival of regular briefings that had petered out during the first term, but she presided over a sea change in White House interactions with journalists.

In February 2025, she stunned the press corps when she announced that the White House itself — and not an independent association of correspondents — would choose which reporters got to cover Trump up close in the Oval Office and on Air Force One.

She also facilitated press credentials from right-wing, pro-Trump media outlets, diluting the presence of traditional news media that tend to ask more challenging questions in the briefing room.

summary.en: Russia's supreme court has banned the anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary elections. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in Russia?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russia's supreme court has banned the anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary elections. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in Russia?

On Monday Russia's supreme court upheld a lawsuit against the anti-war opposition party Yabloko. Its candidates will now be barred from taking part in the parliamentary elections on September 18 to 20.

The case against Yabloko was brought by the pro-Kremlin party Rodina, which accused it of infringing copyright with its election campaign materials. Rodina also made the claim that Yabloko had engaged in extremist activities and had received illegal financing from abroad.

The verdict was pronounced by presiding judge Vyacheslav Kirillov. This was the same judge who, in April, banned the Russian human rights organization Memorial  and designated it an extremist organization. Kirillov also previously dismissed legal complaints against the Russian prison service filed by the prominent opposition politician Alexei Navalny . Navalny spent many years in Russian prisons prior to his death in jail in 2024.

At least 500 people gathered in front of the Supreme Court to show their support for Yabloko. They distributed apples and sang songs. The name Yabloko – "apple" in English – derives from the initials of the party's three founders, Grigory Yavlinsky, Yury Boldyrev and Vladimir Lukin (YaBL). The apple is now well-known as a symbol of the party.

At the end of the nine-hour court session, security services threatened the people gathered outside the courthouse with arrest, also warning young men that they could be taken to an army enlistment office.

"You are mistaken if you believe that, with a stroke of a pen, you can write off millions of people who want peace, freedom and a normal future for their country," Nikolai Rybakov, the leader of Yabloko, wrote on Telegram that evening.

He insisted that the party had not broken any Russian laws, and announced that he would appeal the judgement.

Grigory Yavlinsky, one of the founders of Yabloko, said those in power were afraid of Yabloko's program, which calls for an election "for peace, freedom and a life without fear" – because, he said, "removing a party with a platform like this from the election, without any real grounds, is the political system exposing itself."

The lawsuit came at the same time as an appeal by Russian opposition and cultural leaders living abroad for people to support Yabloko.

They include the politician Yulia Navalnaya , Alexei Navalny's widow, as well as Lyubov Sobol, Ilya Yashin and Andrei Pivovarov. The writer Dmitry Bykov, human rights activist Oleg Orlov and other prominent people also voiced their support for...

title.en: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
title.zh: 奥赫里德协议25周年：北马其顿的和平能否持续？

summary.en: Twenty-five years after the Ohrid Framework Agreement brought an end to North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts caution that peace between the nation's ethnic communities remains delicate.
summary.zh: 在《奥赫里德框架协议》结束北马其顿2001年冲突二十五年后，分析人士警告称，该国各族群之间的和平依然脆弱。

body.en:
A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.

The guns fell silent in 2001, but North Macedonia is still grappling with the legacy of its ethnic conflict.

Twenty-five years after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended the fighting, ethnic Macedonians and Albanians live in peace, yet analysts say genuine reconciliation remains unattained.

The six-month conflict that erupted in February 2001 is often described as the final chapter of former Yugoslavia's violent breakup.

But unlike the wars in Croatia , Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo , it was contained before it could spiral into a larger tragedy, thanks in large part to a political compromise brokered by NATO , the United States and leading EU countries.

Тwenty-five years later, the political order that emerged from the Ohrid Framework Agreement is entering a new phase.

When the conservative Macedonian VMRO-DPMNE party returned to power two years ago , the Democratic Union for Integration (DUI), the main ethnic Albanian party, went into opposition.

This development ended two decades of governing influence for Ali Ahmeti, who transformed himself from leader of the ethnic Albanian National Liberation Army (NLA) during the 2001 conflict into one of the country's most influential political figures.

Ahmeti, who swapped his guerrilla uniform for tailored black suits and white shirts after the Ohrid Agreement, now argues that ethnic relations have deteriorated over the past two years.

"Attacks on the official use of the Albanian language, the abolition of equitable and adequate representation, the weakening of mechanisms designed to prevent majoritarian rule and the promotion of a monoethnic concept of the state are serious signals about the direction in which the country is moving," he said in a statement marking August 2, North Macedonia's national holiday.

Home to a large ethnic Albanian minority, North Macedonia has spent much of the past quarter-century trying to balance its ethnic diversity within a stable political system.

According to the latest census, Albanians make up over a quarter of North Macedonia's population of 1.8 million.

For Bujar Osmani, a senior DUI official and former foreign minister, the key question is no longer how much of the Ohrid Agreement has been implemented, but whether its gains can be preserved.

"On the 25th anniversary of the Ohrid Agreement, the question is no longer only what we have implemented since 2001. The question is whether we will allow, within a few years, the dismantling of what has kept North Macedonia stable for two and a half decades," he told DW.

title.en: No oil, no salary: Iraqi state employees are feeling the crunch of the Hormuz blockade
title.zh: 没有石油，没有工资：伊拉克国家雇员正在感受到霍尔木兹封锁的压力

summary.en: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?

They may be thousands of kilometers away but the Strait of Hormuz — or more specifically, its blockade — is making life increasingly difficult for many ordinary Iraqis.

For the last three months or so, Mahmoud Waleed's salary has been arriving later and later. The 38-year-old teacher is paid by the Iraqi Ministry of Education, but because Iraq cannot export enough oil through the Strait of Hormuz, the government is running out of cash.

"The delay affects you a lot," the Mosul local told DW. "Like most people, we have financial obligations as well as basic living expenses. We're just more and more convinced that we need to reduce expenses and keep some money aside for emergencies — just until things return to normal. It makes you really anxious and fearful."

"The future looks more uncertain," adds Ahmed, a doctor from the same city who didn't want to give DW his full name for personal reasons. "This month, our salaries were delayed by more than 10 days. The Minister of Health explained the state doesn't have sufficient cash flow and that's why there was a delay. But we just don't know how long the next delay will be."

In early August, there were a number of small demonstrations about the delayed salaries. Staff from universities around the country protested as did employees at the Ministry of Electricity.

Almost all of Iraq's national budget, somewhere between 85% and 90%, comes from the export of its oil.

At the same time, Iraq has a huge and growing public sector, with about two-thirds of the around 30 million working-age Iraqis relying on the state for their livelihoods. That's why the majority of the state budget now goes towards salaries, pensions and social welfare; every month the Iraqi government needs somewhere between $6.5 billion and $8.2 billion for those payments.

Since Israel and the US bombed Iran in late February, Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz . Almost all of Iraq's oil — between 80% to 90% — was shipped out through there because unlike other countries in the region, Iraq doesn't have significant alternative routes.

As a result of the blockade, Iraqi oil exports decreased by around 83% in March, compared to the same period last year. By May, Iraq's seaborne crude exports were down 97%.

This means Iraq's national income has also been severely reduced. Government sources told various local media that Iraq's monthly income in May and June was somewhere between $2 billion and $2.3 billion, far less than is needed.

title.en: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
title.zh: 大规模雕像失窃后，莫扎特致敬以酸涩结束

summary.en: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

More than 200 gold-colored Mozart figures have vanished from a public art installation in Salzburg, forcing organizers to end part of the exhibition early.

The theft has disrupted a major public art project marking the 270th anniversary of composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's birth in his home city.

The Mozarteum Foundation said 210 of the 320 figures installed in the city's Mirabell Garden had disappeared. The theft forced organizers to end the garden display early.

Organizers had kept some replacements in reserve, but not enough to offset the scale of the theft.

The manufacturer is also on summer holiday, leaving no quick way to replace them.

Several dozen figures remain on display at the Mozarteum and Mozart 's birthplace until the end of August.

The figures had been placed in the Mirabell Garden and at several Mozart-related sites around Austria's fourth-largest city.

The polymer figures show Mozart with his dog Pimperl, a nod to the composer's everyday life in Salzburg.

German conceptual artist Ottmar Hörl, who is behind the display, said he wanted to show Mozart not as a monument but "as a normal human being despite his genius."

Hörl is known for installations made up of large numbers of identical figures depicting famous personalities.

Hörl said he did not believe tourists had simply walked off with the 50-centimeter (20-inch) figures.

"This is organized theft," he said, suggesting they were probably taken at night after the garden had closed. "I find it a bit cheeky."

Hörl had planned to sell the figures after the exhibition for around €90 each, putting the loss at roughly €20,000.

A previous Hörl display in Bayreuth suffered a similar fate when 100 figures of composer Richard Wagner disappeared.

"That's just the nature of public space," Hörl said. "When you work as an artist in a public space, you mustn't complain about what is happening there. It ranges from destruction to theft. That’s just how it is."

body.zh: 210 个金色雕像从奥地利最繁忙的旅游景点之一消失后，一部向莫扎特致敬的俏皮电影变成了一部侦探小说。大规模盗窃事件迫使组织者提前结束户外展示。 超过 200 个金色莫​​扎特雕像从萨尔茨堡的公共艺术装置中消失，迫使组织者提前结束部分展览。 这起盗窃事件扰乱了其家乡纪念作曲家沃尔夫冈·阿玛多伊斯·莫扎特诞辰 270 周年的大型公共艺术项目。 莫扎特基金会表示，安装在该市米拉贝尔花园的 320 个雕像中，有 210 个失踪了。这起盗窃事件迫使组织者提前结束花园展示。 组织者保留了一些替代品，但不足以抵消盗窃的规模。 制造商也正在放暑假，没有办法快速更换。 直到八月底，莫扎特博物馆和莫扎特的出生地仍展出数十尊雕像。 这些雕像被放置在米拉贝尔花园和奥地利第四大城市周围的几个与莫扎特相关的地点。 聚合物人物展示了莫扎特和他的狗 Pimperl，向作曲家在萨尔茨堡的日常生活致敬。 展览背后的德国概念艺术家奥特马尔·霍尔表示，他不想把莫扎特展示为一座纪念碑，而是“作为一个普通人，尽管他有天才”。 霍尔以由大量描绘名人的相同人物组成的装置而闻名。 霍尔表示，他不相信游客会直接带着这些 50 厘米（20 英寸）的人物走开。 “这是有组织的盗窃行为，”他说，并暗示这些物品可能是在夜间花园关闭后被偷走的。 “我觉得有点厚脸皮。” 霍尔原计划在展览结束后以每件 90 欧元左右的价格出售这些人物模型，这样一来损失就达到了约 20,000 欧元。 之前在拜罗伊特举行的 Hörl 展览也遭遇了类似的命运，作曲家理查德·瓦格纳 (Richard Wagner) 的 100 个雕像消失了。 “这就是公共空间的本质，”霍尔说。 “当你作为一名艺术家在公共场所工作时，你不能抱怨那里发生的事情。它的范围从破坏到盗窃。事情就是这样。” 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Zhu Rongji, who helped turn China into a trading giant, dies at 97
title.zh: 曾帮助中国成为贸易大国的朱镕基去世，享年97岁

summary.en: The former premier brought China into the WTO and championed reforms that fuelled growth.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who spearheaded China's entry into global trade and laid the foundation for its explosive growth, has died at the age of 97.

He served in the country's second-highest office from 1998-2003 and played a leading role in securing its entry into the World Trade Organization, opening Chinese factories to the international market and drawing foreign investment.

He was one of the most important economic reformers who moved local tax powers to the central government, closed or privatised failing state firms and promoted home ownership.

Many in China remember him as a tough and pragmatic leader who delivered double-digit growth and was rarely afraid to speak his mind.

In 1998, he said China was facing "many potential crises that could erupt at any time...

"Ordinary people are discontent about us in many ways. Especially, there is corruption among officials, the gulf between rich and poor and the way some local officials act like tyrants."

He labelled rogue bankers as "half-wits" and said the dams and flood dykes lining the Yangtze River were as "flimsy and porous as tofu dregs".

Under his leadership, which helped stabilise the economy and tackle corruption, China began transforming into a manufacturing powerhouse, leaving behind its status as a Communist outsider.

Though he faced criticism because those reforms also led to 30 million lay-offs over five years, and with huge growth came more inequality.

Chinese state media describe Zhu Rongji's life as one of "revolution, struggle and brilliance".

He was born in the central province of Hunan in 1928 and earned a degree in electrical engineering before joining the civil service.

He joined the Communist Party in 1949, but was purged twice - first after criticising Mao Zedong's economic policies as "irrational" and being labelled a "rightist", and again during the Cultural Revolution.

Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death, and by 1991 had risen to the role of vice-premier in charge of China's economy.

Zhu led China through difficult negotiations to enter the World Trade Organization in 2002.

In state media his obituary described him as an "outstanding member of the Communist Party of China and loyal Commnist fighter... an outstanding leader of the Party and state".
body.zh: 中国前总理朱镕基去世，享年97岁。朱镕基是中国进入全球贸易的带头人，为中国的爆炸性增长奠定了基础。 1998年至2003年，他在中国第二高职位任职，在确保中国加入世界贸易组织、中国工厂向国际市场开放和吸引外国投资方面发挥了主导作用。 他是最重要的经济改革家之一，他将地方税收权力移交给中央政府，关闭或私有化破产的国有企业，并促进住房所有权。 许多中国人都记得他是一位强硬而务实的领导人，实现了两位数的增长，并且从不害怕说出自己的想法。 1998年，他表示中国面临“许多随时可能爆发的潜在危机…… “普通人在很多方面对我们不满。特别是官员腐败、贫富差距和一些地方官员的暴君行为。” 他将流氓银行家称为“笨蛋”，并称长江沿岸的水坝和防洪堤“像豆腐渣一样脆弱、多孔”。 在他的领导下，中国稳定了经济并解决了腐败问题，开始转变为制造业强国，摆脱了共产主义局外人的地位。 但他也面临批评，因为这些改革也导致五年内 3000 万人失业，而且巨大的增长带来了更多的不平等。 中国官方媒体将朱镕基的一生描述为“革命、奋斗、辉煌”的一生。 他 1928 年出生于中部湖南省，在加入公务员队伍之前获得了电气工程学位。 他于1949年加入共产党，但两次遭到清洗——第一次是在批评毛泽东的经济政策“非理性”并被贴上“右派”标签之后，第二次是在文化大革命期间。 毛泽东去世后，朱重回国门，并于 1991 年升任副总理，主管中国经济。 2002年，朱镕基带领中国通过艰难的谈判加入世界贸易组织。 官方媒体的讣告将他描述为“优秀的中国共产党党员、忠诚的共产主义战士……党和国家的杰出领导人”。

reflection.en: The immense power of Typhoon Dolphin reminds us of creation's vulnerability and the deep impact natural forces can have on human lives and infrastructure. In moments when the earth itself seems to groan under the weight of storms, we are called to acknowledge the broader suffering of creation.

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town

summary.en: The Pentagon is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, a move attributed to strategic considerations related to China. The reason for this sudden interest in a town of only 130 people is its role in broader international geopolitical dynamics.
summary.zh: 五角大楼正在澳大利亚新南威尔士州的一个小镇投资5亿美元，此举被认为是与中国相关的战略考量。这个只有130人的小镇突然受到关注，是因为它在全球地缘政治动态中的作用。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

title.en: 130,000 people: One Nation clarifies plan for major migration cut
title.zh: 13万人：一国党澄清大规模移民削减计划

summary.en: A key detail behind One Nation's headline migration pledge has now come into focus.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation has confirmed its plan to significantly limit migration to Australia to 130,000 people a year will be based on the net overseas migration forecast.

Australia's migration level has become one of the most combustible debates in federal politics, as the nation faces a housing shortage and pressure on services, particularly in suburban areas.

Migration experts have warned of the dangers of political parties attempting to blame migrants for a lack of homes , arguing that migrant workforces will be essential to building the required housing stock .

The net overseas migration measure is forecast by projecting how many people will enter and depart the country; it includes returning Australians.

This measure includes visitor and tourist options, family and partner visas, working holidaymakers, skilled migration, plus refugee and humanitarian programs.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Under Labor, net overseas migration reached a record high of 556,000 in 2023, following the COVID-19 pandemic.

But Labor has moved to tighten restrictions, projecting net overseas migration to fall to 225,000 people by the 2027-2028 financial year.

The government is preparing to unveil a plan to wind back migration settings to ensure the net overseas migration forecast is met.

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke was set to unveil that plan at the National Press Club last week — but it was put on hold after cabinet jitters about the political implications of cuts to certain programs.

According to its website, One Nation's policy is "capping visas at 130,000 per year to ease pressure on housing, wages, and infrastructure".

A One Nation spokesperson has confirmed to SBS World News that the cap of 130,000 will be on net overseas migration.

That is a dramatic reduction from the current numbers, which the government maintains would affect a range of visa categories and impede productivity nationwide.

But One Nation leader Pauline Hanson maintains the government has been too reliant on migration to keep the economy going.

Meanwhile, Nationals and senior Liberals have distanced themselves from a figure the Opposition's housing minister suggested cutting immigration to.

Andrew Bragg used a National Press Club speech on Wednesday to argue for a Coalition policy of capping net overseas migration at 180,000.

But Nationals leader Matt Canavan has already cautioned against any moves that would reduce the workforce in regional areas.

On Thursday, Opposition leader Angus Taylor said Bragg was expressing personal views and didn't run the speech by him before he delivered it.

summary.en: Australia's next total solar eclipse will deliver a rare spectacle across parts of the country.

body.en:
As millions turned out to see the total solar eclipse over Europe, some Australians may be wondering when it will be our turn to enjoy such a spectacle.

If you're among them, there's some good news: Australia's next total solar eclipse is on the horizon, and it will bring a rare celestial spectacle to parts of the country.

A total solar eclipse is when the moon's orbit passes between the Earth and the sun. For a few moments, the three planetary bodies align. The moon almost perfectly blocks the sun from view, plunging the planet below into a brief darkness.

That's quite different to the partial solar eclipse. In a partial solar eclipse, the orbits of the Earth, moon, and sun align, but the moon only obscures part of the sun.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's rare for total solar eclipses to happen anywhere. It's rarer still for them to happen in Australia. There have been just five total solar eclipses visible from Australia in the last 50 years — two close together in 1974 and 1976, then long gaps between eclipses in 2002, 2013 and 2023.

Even then, the word "visible" has done some heavy lifting. Most total eclipses only graze the Australian continent, passing over a northern or southern tip. The 2023 total eclipse, for instance, passed just off the North West Cape region of Western Australia and then transited northeast over Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

The 2028 total solar eclipse, also referred to as the Great Australasian Eclipse in some quarters, will start on Saturday 22 July 2028. As the name suggests, the moon will completely obscure the sun for those on the ground.

It will pass south-west across the Australian continent from the Kimberley in northern Western Australia. The eclipse path will then move across the Northern Territory, south-western Queensland and rural NSW, and finally arrive directly over Sydney.

For those in the Kimberley, the total eclipse will begin at around 11am AWST. In Sydney, the total eclipse will start at 2pm AEST. It will last for around four minutes as the moon passes in front of the sun.

To put the rarity of an eclipse path of this kind into context, 2028 will be the first time Sydney has experienced a total solar eclipse since 1857. According to NASA, it won't happen again for another 800 years — 3 June 2858.

When the 2028 eclipse passes over Dunedin in New Zealand later that afternoon, it will be the first to do so since 1163.

body.en:
The Coalition's plan to boost housing stock will involve "trade-offs", a Liberal frontbencher has said, after suggesting low-income households should accept living in substandard homes.

Opposition housing and homelessness spokesperson Andrew Bragg announced on Wednesday that the Opposition would reduce the national housing code from 2,000 pages to 80 if elected.

When asked by ABC Radio National on Thursday morning whether his policy means low-income earners should just accept living in substandard housing, he replied: "Yes, definitely."

He went on to say that building more homes under a streamlined code would come with "trade-offs".

"It's more important to have a house than to not have a house. And so, given the affordability crisis we have in the housing system, we need to just build more houses," he told the ABC.

Bragg's comments follow remarks made by his Liberal colleague and treasury spokesman Tim Wilson, who suggested in some cases people could put "a jumper on in winter rather than spending huge amounts of money" on improving housing quality.

He told ABC RN on Wednesday there should not be a one-size-fits-all policy — such as mandated energy efficiency — for construction.

"There are some places in the country where you will get cold spells or hot spells for a very small amount of the year, whereas for the rest of the year, it's not necessary," he said.

"We have a risk that Australians can't afford to rent or to buy their own home by the government's own budget design. We need housing stock that meets different needs in different environmental conditions. Queensland is not the same as Tasmania or Victoria. Western Australia is different again."

Affordable housing advocates told SBS News that stripping back construction regulations is a way for developers to profit from "unliveable" homes.

"Too many renters are already living in homes that are freezing in winter, stifling in summer, riddled with mould and damp, and expensive to heat and cool," Everybody's Home spokesperson Maiy Azize said in a statement.

"Older people and people with disability already struggle to find homes they can safely and comfortably live in."

Azize added that the government should focus on social housing that is "built to last".

"We have a housing crisis because people cannot afford a home. Building more poor-quality homes does nothing to fix that crisis. It simply gives developers another way to profit from it," Azize said.

Australian Council of Social Services CEO Dr Cassandra Goldie agreed, adding that construction of social housing should "drastically scale up".

body.en:
Whistleblower David McBride has avoided political questions on the day of his release from prison, instead making a quick getaway to see his beloved dog.

The 62-year-old was released after more than two years behind bars following a successful parole bid.

"I'm very happy to be out. It's a beautiful day to be free," he said, speaking to media from a car on his way out of Canberra's Alexander Maconochie Centre on Thursday.

The former army lawyer was sentenced to a maximum of five years and eight months in jail in May 2024 after he helped steal secret defence documents about the Afghanistan war. He then leaked them to the media.

His parole was considered and granted on Thursday morning, a spokesperson for Attorney-General Michelle Rowland said.

"It's so good to see the end of an awful saga that should never have happened. I salute David, who walks away from prison with his head held high," he said.

McBride had aimed to expose excessive investigation of Australian soldiers in Afghanistan, but it was revealed soon after that defence personnel had been involved in illegal killings while on the front lines. He pleaded guilty to three charges, including theft.

"I'm looking forward to seeing my dog and my daughters ... hopefully my dog will remember who I am," he said upon release.

He declined to answer questions about Australia's whistleblower laws, saying he wanted to be fair to Rowland, who had just approved his parole.

McBride will be allowed to serve the last three years of his sentence in the community under supervision and strict conditions.

The news was celebrated by Greens senator David Shoebridge, who said McBride should have walked free long ago.

"My friend David McBride has paid a terrible price for saying the truth. It's a price no whistleblower should ever be made to pay again," Shoebridge said in a statement.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
For millions of Australians, deciding who gets their superannuation when they die may be more complicated than simply leaving instructions in a will.

The issue was thrust into the spotlight this week when research from consumer group, Super Consumers Australia, estimated more than 15.5 million Australians do not have a binding death benefit nomination , leaving them without certainty over who will receive their nest egg after their death.

And even where they are available, the rules around who can receive superannuation death benefits can create complications for families that don't fit the traditional spouse-and-children model.

Jessica Spence, director of policy at Super Consumers Australia, said many people mistakenly believe their super will automatically be transferred through their will.

"There are a lot of rules around who you can nominate, and they're a bit confusing, so a lot of people think that they've dealt with it when actually they haven't," she told SBS News.

Generally, a binding death benefit nomination can only name people who fall within certain categories, such as a spouse or child, or someone who meets the requirements of an interdependency relationship.

Spence said for people with family overseas, or relatives who don't meet the definition of a dependant, it complicates who they can actually nominate.

"You have to make a separate nomination to your super fund in order to tell your super fund where you want your super to go after you pass away," she said.

Experts say another option is to nominate a legal personal representative, allowing the super to form part of the estate and be distributed in accordance with the person's will.

But this process can create particular complications for people whose closest family members live abroad, including in cases where they financially support parents, siblings or other relatives.

They also warn that simply nominating someone doesn't always guarantee they will receive your super.

Associate professor Natalie Silver from the University of Sydney researches superannuation as a form of inheritance.

Her research has examined what happens when a death benefit decision is challenged, and the extent to which a deceased person's wishes are ultimately reflected in the outcome.

As Anthony Albanese's weeks-old comments about melons continue to fuel political drama , the fruit at the centre of the controversy has largely been overlooked.

Yet the crown melons gifted to the prime minister by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are no ordinary fruit.

During an appearance on Nikki Osborne's Deep Bush podcast last month, Albanese described the melons as a "pretty strange" gift before praising their quality.

Hand gestures he made while discussing the fruit have since drawn criticism, an interpretation his office has rejected.

Waka Ikeda, writing in the Japan Times, describes a crown melon as "perfection, based on the Japanese artisan spirit of takumi" — something you bring when you wish to honour someone. Her op-ed highlighting Albanese's comments on the podcast kickstarted the furore that has spilled over onto the international stage

Gwyn McClelland, senior lecturer in Japanese studies and president of the Japanese Studies Association of Australia, told SBS News that he shared the Japan Times story with his students to express how "incensed" he was by the prime minister's gesture.

"I was just really annoyed that he didn't realise the giving of fruit could be really lovely and important," he said.

"In an Australian context, that doesn't look like an amazing gift, necessarily ... [but] I was upset that Albanese hadn't thought about gift-giving culture because it is very central in Japan.

Eri Dennis, former officer at the Australian embassy in Tokyo and current cultural consultant at manufacturing consultancy Shinka Management, told SBS News the practice is deeply ingrained and "definitely an important part of our culture".

"Whenever we visit someone, even a family member or your friend, for some significant occasion, or if you haven't met them for some time, it's just a natural part of our culture that we bring along gifts," she said. "It doesn't have to be an expensive gift, but it's a gesture that we care about you."

title.en: New twist in Australia's bird flu battle amid 'extinction-level impact' warning
title.zh: 澳大利亚禽流感之战出现“灭绝级别影响”警告的新转折

body.en:
Scientists have warned that Australia's H5N1 outbreak could take a new turn if the virus mixes with local bird flu strains.

CSIRO scientists analysing bird flu virus samples are watching for signs the deadly H5N1 strain has swapped genetic material with influenza viruses already circulating in Australian birds.

The process could produce new strains capable of infecting a broader range of bird species, though scientists stress this has not yet been detected in Australia and the potential impacts of any new strain cannot be predicted.

They have also warned the virus could have an "extinction-level impact" on some of Australia's most vulnerable species, while acknowledging there are limits to how many wild animals can be protected through vaccination.

When different influenza strains infect the same host, those segments can be exchanged through a process known as reassortment, creating a virus with a new combination of genes.

CSIRO senior research scientist Dr Frank Wong said this process had occurred as H5N1 spread around the world, with the virus picking up genetic material from local bird flu viruses.

"When a virus goes to a new area and it picks up gene segments from local viruses, it could provide the new genotype or new strain with better host fitness for host species in that new area," he said.

That could mean the virus becomes better suited to infecting new bird species or a broader range of birds.

Wong said reassortment could occur in Australia, which is why scientists are continuing to track the virus, but its potential impact would be difficult to predict.

CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness is using whole genome sequencing to monitor the virus and identify changes as more samples are collected.

Sequencing team leader Dr Matthew Nieve said scientists were specifically looking for signs the H5N1 virus introduced to Australia, known as genotype B3.2, had "switched up one of its genes with a local low path Australian virus".

Scientists are also looking for mutations that could indicate changes in the virus which allow it to infect mammals more readily.

So far, sequencing suggests the virus has entered mainland Australia multiple times, with CSIRO detecting at least six or seven separate introduction events believed to have originated from Heard Island, which is about 4,100km south-west of Perth.

Nieve said that figure was likely an underestimate because it only included incursions that had been detected and sampled.

But the sequencing shows a different pattern among some Australian resident birds.

body.en:
Working full-time hours in retail and hospitality while undertaking her degree, she said she has been forced to return to her Brisbane family home while she tries to save a deposit to eventually buy a property.

But rising everyday costs mean saving is difficult, leaving her feeling as though the traditional path into adulthood is becoming increasingly out of reach.

"I feel like I'm doing everything you're told you're supposed to do. I'm working, I'm studying, I'm saving when I can," she told SBS News.

Sophie's experience reflects a broader trend identified in a new five-year analysis of the Australian Youth Barometer.

The Monash Centre for Youth Policy and Education Practice has tracked more than 2,700 Australians aged 18 to 24 since 2021, examining their experiences across work, education, housing, wellbeing, relationships and civic participation.

Its latest report describes young Australians as living through a "polycrisis" of overlapping economic, social, environmental and political pressures that compound one another.

Affordable housing was the biggest issue young people flagged as needing urgent action, rising from 60 per cent in 2022 to 82 per cent in 2025.

Also recognised as needing urgent action was employment opportunities, which rose from 48 in 2022 to 64 per cent in 2025. Climate change was identified as an issue needing urgent action by 44 per cent in 2025, falling from 47 per cent in 2022.

Monash University professor Lucas Walsh, the report's lead author, says the significance of the findings is in how those issues connect.

"These are all embedded within the idea of a polycrisis, which involves overlapping independent events in crisis that intersect and amplify each other," he told SBS News.

Walsh said the study started tracking young Australians at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, providing a five-year window into how their lives and priorities have changed as the country moved through and beyond it.

He describes the pandemic as a "flash of light into more persistent problems" which exposed pressures that were already disproportionately affecting young people.

"I don't necessarily expect to own a house tomorrow, but I would like to feel like it's something I could realistically work towards. It can be discouraging to feel like the goalposts for how much I need to have saved, how much I need to be earning or even spending to get a home keeps changing," she said.

Wendy Stone, a professor of housing and social policy at Swinburne University, told SBS News that secure housing provides the foundation that young people need to establish independence, work, study and relationships.

body.en:
The Fair Work Commission has issued a new minimum standards order for gig workers, including on-demand food, beverage and grocery delivery drivers.

The standards, released on Tuesday, stipulate that on-demand delivery workers must be paid a minimum rate of $31.30 or up to $32 per hour, depending on the type of vehicle used. The order also specifies that delivery platforms must insure workers for on-the-job injuries.

The Transport Workers' Union (TWU), which represents Australian gig workers, said these changes have been years in the making . The TWU initially applied for the minimum standards order in 2024, alongside food delivery platforms Uber Eats and DoorDash.

In a joint statement provided to SBS News, TWU national secretary Michael Kaine described the new standards as "world-leading".

"The world is looking on as gig workers in Australia win new rights and protections that will change their lives, after years of campaigning for a better industry," Kaine said.

Employment and Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth also believes the order is a "big step" in providing more robust worker protections .

She said it means "food and delivery workers don't have to trade off flexibility for fairer protections".

The TWU said "hundreds of thousands" of delivery workers in Australia will be impacted by the new orders.

They specifically apply to employee-like workers who are engaged through digital on-demand delivery platforms — such as Uber Eats and DoorDash — and mainly deliver consumables (food, beverages or liquor) or supermarket groceries .

These workers will be entitled to a guaranteed minimum hourly rate for their "engaged time" between accepting an order and completing the delivery. This is also called an "earnings floor".

People operating bicycles or e-bikes will be paid $31.30 an hour. For motorbikes, this increases to $31.80 per hour, and workers driving cars will earn $32 per hour.

According to the interim order, platforms will calculate a worker's total earnings over a period of up to 21 days. If a worker "has been paid less than the earnings floor in an earnings period, the digital labour platform operator will pay a top-up amount to ... make up the difference", it said.
